title: On Including the name in the list
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：include　|　正文 353 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 include 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1992 the tailor ① included the name in the list without a word of thanks, and every customer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the tailor ② includes the name in the list at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ include the name in the list at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ included the name in the list before — a line in the order for November 1986 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Including the name in the list without a word of thanks, the tailor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ include a postscript about the money at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Include a postscript about the money at once and never mention it again.

By 1999 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the order, and a new customer from the next shop ⑧ includes a postscript about the money without a word of thanks every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the mirror, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ included the name in the list again when nobody else would.

⑩ To include the name in the list, my mother said in 2004, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody includes the name in the list at once again and somebody must include the name in the list without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 列入（一般过去式 included the name in the list：1992 年裁缝头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 列入（一般现在 includes the name in the list：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 列入（不定式 to include the name in the list：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 列入（过去完成时 had included the name in the list：1986 年十一月的订单簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 列入（动名词 including the name in the list 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 包含（include a postscript about the money：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去包含附上一段关于钱的话）
G. v. 包含（include a postscript about the money：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 列入（后段两处：新来的顾客照例 includes a postscript about the money，而母亲又一次 included the name in the list）

answers.why: include 意为“列入”，1992 年裁缝不图一句谢列入把那个名字列进单子，那是裁缝铺里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 included。
include 意为“列入”，自那以后裁缝二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 includes。
include 意为“列入”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯列入把那个名字列进单子”，此处为不定式 to include the name in the list。
include 意为“列入”，订单簿里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1999 年之前就有人列入过，故用过去完成时 had included。
include 意为“列入”，裁缝说“列入把那个名字列进单子这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 including the name in the list 作主语。
include 意为“包含”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去包含附上一段关于钱的话”，should ever 之后用原形 include a postscript about the money。
include 意为“包含”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻包含附上一段关于钱的话（include a postscript about the money at once），以后再也不要提起。
include 意为“列入”，新来的顾客每个星期都照例包含附上一段关于钱的话，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 includes。
include 意为“列入”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢列入把那个名字列进单子，用一般过去式 included 叙述。
include 意为“列入”，结尾那句是母亲 2004 年的话：要列入把那个名字列进单子，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和裁缝铺记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 include 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1992 the tailor included the name in the list without a word of thanks, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the tailor includes the name in the list at once whenever the shop asks.
Including the name in the list without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever include a postscript about the money at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new customer from the next shop includes a postscript about the money without a word of thanks every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother included the name in the list again, and the shop remembered that half.
